column1: # tools/binsim-corpus.tsv -- the six trees `tools/binsim.py --corpus` scores.
# The bytes never enter this repository: they are someone else's property and
# one of the six is this unit's own flash dump. What is committed is the
# manifest, so a run that scored a DIFFERENT file is refused instead of
# reported. `binsim.py` checks length and sha256 in `check_integrity()` before it
# reads a single instruction -- it did NOT until 2026-08-27, when the check ran
# after the ELF had already been parsed and tokenised while this line said
# otherwise. `D1` exercises that same function three ways, and
# `tools/test-binsim.sh` drives the whole path with a corrupted manifest and with
# a corpus file truncated in its body; the second used to crash inside `tokenize`
# and exit 1, the code reserved for "reported, but a result is void".
# `--check-manifest` parses and validates THIS file with no vendor byte present,
# which is how a runner reaches it at all: before that mode existed the only
# reader was `--corpus`, and a typo in `@floor` would have surfaced on one
# machine months later.
# Files live at   $FWRE_WORK/extracted/<tree>/squashfs-root/<relpath>
# override with   --root DIR
# Columns, tab separated:
#   tree  built  program  relpath  bytes  sha256  role
# `built` is the timestamp in that tree's BusyBox banner -- INSIDE the image,
# not a filesystem attribute a copy could destroy. It corroborates the mtimes,
# though NOT to within ten minutes in all six trees as this line first claimed:
# 量 2026-08-27 the banner-to-mtime gap runs 2m02s to 1h48m02s, and v3.4.0 is the
# outlier at 1h48m (163 files stamped 11:43 against a 09:55:29 banner) with
# v2.1.2 marginal at 10m04s. It is packaging lag, systematic per tree, and it
# does not touch the date. What matters is that it is the
# BUILD date, which is not the vendor's RELEASE date: `SPEC.md` `FW-19` and
# `notes/lwl-mystery.md` both carry 2015-08-25 for `v2.1.2` in a column headed
# `build`, and 2015-08-25 is upstream's release date for that firmware. The
# image says 2015-08-11 17:26:34 CST in the banner and 2015-08-11 17:36:38 in
# every mtime.
# `role` is what the corpus uses the program for:
#   subject   the plan's failure condition applies -- if its pairwise scores
#             span less than five percentage points its numbers are void
#   identity  a program that is byte-identical in every tree. `bin/acltd` is
#             one sha256 across all six -- 10,032 bytes, `.comment` `GCC: (GNU)
#             3.2.3-1.2.11`, a prebuilt blob carried unchanged for five years
#             across three product lines. It is the identity anchor AND the
#             positive control on the void verdict, whose fifteen cells span
#             exactly zero. A verdict that never fires is not a verdict.
# It is also the trap in this corpus: `grep 'GCC: (GNU)' unit-2018/` answers
# 3.2.3-1.2.11, and that is acltd's compiler, not this unit's. Only the two
# 2015/2016 trees still carry a `.comment` for their own `boa`, and it reads
# MEMBERSHIP RULE, and it is enforced by control E0 rather than left here.
# A tree belongs in this corpus only if its binaries are the SAME ISA as this
# unit's: ELF32, big-endian (MSB), EM_MIPS, `e_flags` arch field 0 (MIPS-I).
# E0 refuses a corpus that mixes them and names the odd one out.
# The rule exists because the question came up with a real image. 量 2026-08-27,
# `TOTOLINK-N350RT_V9.3.5u.6466_B20250825`, a 2025 release for a TOTOLINK
# product with a neighbouring model number:
#   container       U-Boot legacy uImage (magic 27051956), image name C8351R-6466
#                   -- not the Realtek loader container the other six use
#   SoC             **MediaTek MT7628**, named in the kernel image
#   kernel          Linux 3.4.113, gcc 4.4.7, built 2025-08-25
#   rootfs          little-endian SquashFS 4.0 (`hsqs`), xz, at offset 1,044,416
#   /bin/busybox    ELF 32-bit **LSB**, MIPS32 rel2, e_flags 0x70001007
#   libc            uClibc 0.9.33.2
#   web server      lighttpd. There is no `boa` in it at all
# Against this unit: big-endian MIPS-I, e_flags 0x1007, Linux 2.6.30.9, uClibc
# 0.9.30.3, boa. Different endianness, different ISA level, different SoC
# vendor, different bootloader, different kernel line, different web server.
# `binsim.py` refuses it before scoring -- `ELF data 1, not MSB (big-endian)`,
# exit 2 -- and a seventh tree would have added nothing to a matrix about which
# Realtek GPL drop built a Lexra-core device.
# Recorded rather than dropped, because "we looked and it is a different part"
# is a result, and because the model numbering does NOT imply a shared platform.
# @base and @floor name the two cells `plan/router-rebuild-plan.md:1128` defines
# as the thresholds. They are cells of the matrix, not numbers anyone chose.
# binsim reports the FLOOR cell as REFUTED when it lands below the score of two
# DIFFERENT PROGRAMS from one tree, which is what it does here -- naming a
# replacement is R2a/b/d-1's decision and not this file's.
@base
@floor
